title: Workload Orthogonalizer — benchmark harness for continuous batching and queueing interference
creator: Ravi Narayanan
description:
Objective: build a portable, configurable benchmarking harness (the 'Workload Orthogonalizer') that isolates orthogonal workload axes to quantify how continuous batching and request queueing interact under mixed tenant profiles. We want to capture both steady-state tokens/sec and tail behavior (p95/p99) as workload composition changes (short vs long tokens, KV cache locality, multi-model mixes, and arrival burstiness).

Scope: harness generates parametrized arrival processes (Poisson, bursty waveforms, bimodal sessions) with per-session affinity to model variants and KV prefix reuse. The harness instruments queue depth, batch size distribution, batch occupancy, tokens/sec, token latency percentiles, and per-request KV hit/miss counters. It should produce telemetry consumable by Console dashboards and Regression pipelines.

Why different from previous probes: existing suites focus on mixed arrival profiling or synthetic queueing probes. Orthogonalizer explicitly composes axes (token-length, reuse-locality, concurrency, model-heterogeneity) and sweeps them in factorial designs to attribute non-linear interactions (e.g., small-long token mixes causing batch fragmentation and p95 amplification). We will adopt analysis techniques from design-of-experiments to quantify interaction terms rather than single-dimension sweeps.

Approach: implement both a lightweight replay mode (capture real production traces and replay with controlled reshaping) and a synthetic generator mode (parameterized RNG with seeds for reproducibility). Provide a profiling adapter for the runtime to emit per-batch metadata via existing tracing hooks. Results will be ingested into a standardized dashboard and regression detector (statistical tests on p95 shifts and tokens/sec deltas).

Success metrics: harness runs end-to-end in CI and can reproduce two known regressions (ENG-3147 tokenflow p95 drift and ENG-44678 bimodal tail). Baseline runs for two model families (redwood-7B and opensource-13B q8) and three workload mixes produced and stored as reference artifacts.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can replay a captured 30-minute traffic trace with configurable reshaping parameters and reproduce baseline p95 within ±5%
Synthetic generator supports at least four axes: token_length_distribution, session_affinity, kv_reuse_probability, model_mix_ratio
Per-batch metadata (batch_size, batch_latency_ms, kv_hits) exported to existing telemetry schema and visible in an experiment dashboard
Automated regression job can run harness in CI and flag p95 regressions using bootstrap-based confidence intervals
Documentation and a runnable example present in the repo with a minimal Docker run command
test_plan: Phase 1 (spike, 1 week): prototype generator + adapter that talks to local runtime stub. Produce synthetic mix and verify batch-level events.
Phase 2 (validation, 2 weeks): integrate with capture-replay traces from staging, run factorial sweeps and compute interaction coefficients; compare to baseline artifacts.
Phase 3 (automation, 1 week): CI integration, dashboard ingestion, and regression gating with thresholding and notification to #perf-alerts.
Phase 4 (docs, 1 week): write how-to guide, export templates for common profiles (PLG webchat, backend LLM-assistant, embeddings-heavy), and handoff to SRE and Console teams.
